summary: When a hero applies a lock pick toward a closed-door mimic, lock.c:pick_lock reveals it and then calls steal.c:maybe_absorb_item(mon, pick, 50, 10). That helper queries zap.c:obj_resists before deciding whether to absorb the tool. JavaScript lock.js currently skips the helper with note_unported, so it misses C’s rn2(100) draw and leaves a one-call RNG offset while all 114 screens and cursors still match. Port the helper to steal.js and wire this existing lock.js branch in source order.

source.branch: After lock.c:pick_lock finds a monster mimicking a door, it first calls stumble_onto_mimic(), then maybe_absorb_item(mon, pick, 50, 10). For a non-ball, non-chain, non-rock object, maybe_absorb_item calls obj_resists(obj, 50, 90); if that returns true, it returns before touch_artifact() and object transfer. The v39 lock pick is ordinary and C rn2(100)=19, so the resistance branch returns true.
callers: lock.c:pick_lock() at the is_door_mappear() branch (571-576); production dispatch is apply.c:doapply() -> pick_lock().
dependencies: zap.c:obj_resists() is already implemented in js/bury.js; it draws rn2(100) for an ordinary object and uses the ordinary/artifact threshold.

artifact.c:touch_artifact(), steal.c:remove_worn_item()/mpickobj(), invent.c:freeinv(), shk.c:shop_keeper()/subfrombill(), pickup.c:encumber_msg(), vision.c:cansee(), display.c:canspotmon(), and the existing naming/body-part helpers are already implemented.

evidence: The refreshed combined queue SHA-256 is b5fc8af455f088103a8a4b2dbda24754969c97cec080c93d9ea601f8aab53169. Its v39 evaluation is accepted-9576b4f8da10054320739b6775b11284c33b01ed-v39.json; the case has 0 remaining screen mismatches, 114/114 screens, 114/114 cursors, and 6543/6551 RNG calls.

Fresh C/JavaScript differential `.cache/B215-diff-counted.log` reproduces the first RNG divergence at segment 1, step 114, key h: C calls rn2(100)=19 from obj_resists(zap.c:1469); JavaScript has rn2(5)=4 from distfleeck(monmove.c:538). C has one additional RNG call, and the later shifted values account for the remaining unmatched RNG entries.

Upstream lock.c:571-576 executes stumble_onto_mimic(mtmp) followed by maybe_absorb_item(mtmp, pick, 50, 10) when the selected square contains a door-mimicking monster. This is the only maybe_absorb_item call site found in upstream C.

Upstream steal.c:772-810 first excludes uball, uchain, and ROCK_CLASS, then calls obj_resists(obj, 100 - ochance, 100 - achance), then touch_artifact(). If the object resists, the function returns before inventory removal, messages, or mpickobj(). For this recipe the lock pick has ordinary 50% resistance and C’s 19 result returns early.

JavaScript lock.js:845-848 follows the same mimic branch and reveal order but calls note_unported("steal.c maybe_absorb_item") instead of the C helper. The existing obj_resists implementation in js/bury.js already has the source-matched rn2(100) behavior; this task wires it through the missing steal.c caller.
